what_its_for: Febuxostat is used to lower high uric acid levels in adults who have gout. Too much uric acid in your body can form crystals in your joints, causing painful gout attacks. This medicine helps prevent these attacks by keeping uric acid levels under control. It is not used to treat a gout attack that is already happening.
how_to_take: Take febuxostat by mouth, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist says it is okay. Keep taking this medicine even if you have a gout flare-up while starting treatment, as this is common in the beginning.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 40 mg once daily. After about 2 weeks, your doctor may check your uric acid level and increase your dose to 80 mg once daily if needed. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions for your dose. Do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store febuxostat at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking azathioprine or mercaptopurine while on febuxostat, as this combination can be very dangerous — always tell your doctor and pharmacist about all medicines you take. Limit alcohol, as it can raise uric acid levels and make gout worse. Avoid foods high in purines such as organ meats (liver, kidneys), anchovies, sardines, and shellfish, as these can increase uric acid. Do not start this medicine if you are also taking theophylline without checking with your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you have: chest pain, shortness of breath, or symptoms of a heart attack or stroke; a severe skin rash, blisters, or peeling skin; signs of an allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing; yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or stomach pain (signs of liver problems); or numbness or weakness on one side of your body. Also call your doctor if your gout attacks get worse or do not improve, or if you have unusual tiredness.
when_it_works: Febuxostat starts lowering your uric acid levels within a few days, but it may take several weeks to months before you see a full benefit and gout attacks become less frequent. During the first few months of treatment, you may actually have more gout flares than usual — this is normal and does not mean the medicine is not working. Your doctor may prescribe another medicine (such as colchicine or naproxen) to help prevent these early flare-ups. Do not stop taking febuxostat without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women: The safety of febuxostat during pregnancy or breastfeeding is not well known. Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to monitor you more closely or adjust your dose if you have moderate kidney or liver disease. This medicine is generally not recommended for people with severe kidney or liver disease. Older adults: No specific dose changes are needed for older adults, but your doctor will monitor you carefully. Children: Febuxostat is not approved for use in children under 18 years of age.
